text:
The strongest refutation is that pleasures differ in quality, not just quantity. Bentham's calculus counts only intensity, duration and similar quantitative measures, so it can't distinguish higher pleasures from base ones, and that is Mill's classic objection. The other option, that pain and pleasure are inevitable in life, doesn't undermine the calculus, because the calculus only weighs pleasure and pain and never claims we can avoid them.

CONFIDENCE: 80
